articles.title: Amanda Serrano: Seven-weight boxing champion to end career in Puerto Rico in January
articles.summary: Amanda Serrano will face Skye Falzon in Puerto Rico on 9 January in the final fight of her illustrious professional boxing career.
articles.body:
Seven-weight world champion Amanda Serrano will face Australia's Skye Falzon in Puerto Rico on 9 January in the final fight of her illustrious professional boxing career.

The 38-year-old will defend her WBA and WBO featherweight titles on home soil at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico in San Juan.

Serrano, who boasts a fight history of 50 wins, four defeats and one draw, will be seeking to break the all-time women's knockout record in her farewell bout.

"Boxing has been my life, and I never could have imagined the journey it would take me and my family on," said Serrano, who turned professional in 2009.

"To close my career at home in Puerto Rico, in front of the people who have supported me from the beginning, means everything. I'm going to give the fans one final night to remember."

Serrano's farewell bout, labelled The Last Walk, will be contested over 12 three-minute rounds against 37-year-old Falzon, who has won 12 of her 14 professional fights, including seven by knockout.

In her previous outing, Serrano edged a majority decision victory over Argentina's Lucrecia Manzur to claim her 50th professional win.

The contest was the first world title fight to be broadcast live on TikTok, generating 3.4m views.

But Serrano was unable to secure the knockout she needed to surpass American boxing pioneer Christy Martin's record of 32, leaving her with one final opportunity to make history.

'I'll continue fighting for the next generation'

Serrano is the only Puerto Rican boxer, male or female, to become an undisputed world champion.

Her profile reached new heights after she became the first fighter to sign with Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) in 2021.

Founded by YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian, MVP has invested heavily in women's boxing in recent years.

"Nakisa, Jake and MVP believed in me and in women's boxing, and together we've helped change what's possible for women in this sport," Serrano said.

"We've fought for respect, equal opportunities, fair pay, and the choice to compete under the same rules as men.

"There's still more work to do, and I'll continue fighting for the next generation long after I hang up my gloves."

Serrano's career will perhaps be best remembered for her historic rivalry with Ireland's Katie Taylor, who won all three of their encounters.

The pair became the first women to headline a boxing event at the iconic Madison Square Garden in 2022, before meeting again in a hugely watched rematch on Netflix in 2024.

Taylor completed a clean sweep of the trilogy in July 2025, headlining an all-women's card in New York, before retiring in September this year following victory over Flora Pili at Dublin's Croke Park.

Paul and Bidarian said Serrano had "changed the entire landscape of women's boxing".

"Amanda Serrano is the MOAT. The Most Of All Time. The most accomplished female boxer of all time, the most watched, the most paid, and one of the most influential athletes this sport has ever seen," they added.

articles.title: Boxing Federation of India mess: Ajay Singh's rival faction meets Raksha Khadse, IOA CEO; alleges support of 27 units
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid an ongoing political tussle, the Boxing Federation of India's (BFI) affiliaited units and executive committee (ExCo) members sat in one
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid an ongoing political tussle, the Boxing Federation of India's (BFI) affiliaited units and executive committee (ExCo) members sat in one room on Wednesday in New Delhi to showcase their unity and strength against the current president, Ajay Singh. Claiming the support of 27 out of 35 units and 8 of 13 ExCo members, the faction met Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) CEO Raghuram Iyer to register their concerns via a memorandum.It was originally scheduled to be a Special General Meeting (SGM) and vote of no-confidence against Singh. Those plans were shelved by the Punjab and Haryana High Court, which put the SGM in abeyance until November 13.That, however, didn't dissuade the hierarchy from coming together and expressing their displeasure with the three-time BFI president and his tenure.BFI secretary general Pramod Kumar - who was suspended by Singh - treasurer Pon Baskaran, vice-president Rajesh Bhandari, Delhi Amateur Boxing Association vice-president Rohit Jain and others said they submitted a memorandum to the Sports Ministry, the IOA and World Boxing president Gennadiy Golovkin.The memorandum accused Singh of concentrating powers in his hands, sidelining elected office-bearers and undermining democratic processes within the federation.Separately, the group alleged administrative lapses, disregard for the constitution and a “Hitler-ish approach” by Singh."We have given our memorandum to them (Sports Ministry). Whatever issued we have, whether it is related to the constitution or technical conduct, whether it is related to coaching or selection committee, and about the administration, we have told him everything. Now, it is his decision. And we have also written to the global body. Unfortunately, the meeting we wanted to hold today wasn't possible, but let's see what changes from here," said Bhandari."Every time an official within the Boxing Federation has questioned Ajay Singh's authority, they have either been suspended or served with a show-cause notice. If we do not get any respite from this situation, it is possible that we will sit at Jantar Mantar in the coming days," said BFI Senior VP Rajesh Bhandari.Rohit Jain, who has challenged Singh's presidency in the past and vows to do so again, claimed the biggest issue is the constitutional overreach."This battle started in 2024. They modified the constitution as such that it suits them. They rested all the powers at the seat of the president. They suspend any state unit without giving a notice, without assigning any reasons. Have you ever heard that someone will be suspended without giving a reason and an ad-hoc committee be formed? The main reason for this, I have to say, is that I have experienced the pain. They wanted to keep me away from boxing and competition so that I could not win the elections and could not stand in front of them. They changed the constitution not once, but twice," he said.BFI claims support of 21 authorised unitsOn the same day, 21 of BFI's 35 authorised state units participated in a two-day ‘Mission Olympic Podium’ meeting in Bagdogra. Representatives of 18 units attended in person, while three joined through video conferencing. The participating units included the ad hoc committees of Mizoram and Jharkhand along with the BFI Athletes committee player representative.“Our responsibility is to the boxers and their future. The participation of a majority of our authorised state units demonstrates their commitment to working together as a federation towards our Olympic ambitions, with athletes at the centre of that effort. The work begins in the states — identifying talent, supporting coaches and creating a clear pathway for boxers to progress, gain competitive exposure and represent India. We must build a system that consistently prepares our boxers to succeed at the highest level,” said BFI chief Ajay Singh.The latest developments come as the administrative chaos in the BFI continues for a third year running. The current logjam was heightened after Ajay Singh suspended Pramod Kumar, who had challenged the president’s authority. Singh has argued that his removal will require support from three-fourths of the General Body members. But for that, SGM needs to be called as per the constitutional norms. Meanwhile, for a no-confidence vote against Singh to succeed, the rival faction needs support of 23 units, or two-thirds.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Adam Azim: Briton to face Gabriel Gollaz Valenzuela on 4 December
articles.summary: British light-welterweight Adam Azim is set to face Gabriel Gollaz Valenzuela at London's Copper Box on 4 December.
articles.body:
British light-welterweight Adam Azim is set to face Gabriel Gollaz Valenzuela at London's Copper Box on 4 December.

Azim last fought in May when he stopped Steve Claggett in three rounds at Wembley Arena live on BBC Two.

The 24-year-old is undefeated in 15 professional fights, winning 12 by stoppage, while Mexico's Valenzuela holds a record of 32 wins, five losses and one draw.

BBC Sport understands the bout will serve as an IBF title eliminator, with the winner in line to challenge for the belt in early 2027.

Azim, who made his professional debut in 2020, has won each of his last six fights by knockout.

Valenzuela has lost two previous world title eliminator fights against Subriel Matias and Lindolfo Delgado in 2025.

The 32-year-old has earned 18 of his 32 wins by stoppage, including a knockout win in his last fight in May.

The IBF title is currently vacant after former champion Richardson Hitchins moved up to to welterweight after signing with Zuffa Boxing.

Delgado and Russian-Canadian Arthur Biyarslanov were due to compete for the vacant belt on Saturday but the Mexican withdrew earlier this week with his team citing safety concerns for the bout on the undercard of Christian Mbilli v Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez in Saudi Arabia.

Azim has long been linked with WBC light-welterweight champion Dalton Smith and victory would keep an all-British bout on track for 2027.

articles.summary: Amanda Serrano's legendary boxing career will come to an end on Jan. 9.
articles.body:
Amanda Serrano's legendary boxing career will come to an end on Jan. 9.

Most Valuable Promotions announced on Wednesday that Serrano will challenge Skye Falzon for the unified featherweight world championship in her retirement fight at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico.

Unlike traditional women's boxing matches consisting of 10 two-minute rounds, the Serrano-Falzon bout will be contested under men's rules with 12 three-minute rounds.

The Real Deal has experience in this format, as her 2023 matchup with Danila Ramos was the first women's unified championship fight to feature 12 three-minute rounds.

Serrano posted a statement on X about her final bout:

The matchup with Falzon will mark Serrano's 56th career boxing match. She is 50-4-1 through her first 55 bouts and has never lost via knockout/TKO.

Since her back-to-back losses against Katie Taylor, Serrano has won each of her last three fights.

Serrano's 32 career knockout wins are tied with Christy Martin for the most ever by a women's boxer. She said after equaling the mark with a second-round TKO against Cheyenne Hanson that surpassing Martin's record was something she was chasing.

"I can break the knockout record in my next fight," Serrano said. "I can get my 50th win and break Christy Martin's knockout record."

Serrano was unable to surpass the KO mark in her most recent fight, but she did get to win No. 50 by defeating Lucrecia Anabella Manzur via majority decision to retain the WBA, WBO, and The Ring featherweight titles on Aug. 21.

Falzon is 12-2 with seven knockout wins in her career. Her most recent appearance was a win over Monika Singh on Sept. 17 to win the WBA Oceania and WBA Asia women's featherweight championships.

articles.title: Raven Chapman: Boxer on brain bleed and road to recovery
articles.summary: Boxer Raven Chapman reveals that the fast actions of trainer Stuart Scott may have saved her life when she suffered a bleed on the brain over the summer.
articles.body:
Boxer Raven Chapman believes the fast actions of trainer Stuart Scott may have saved her life when she suffered a bleed on the brain over the summer.

The 32-year-old was airlifted to hospital and placed in a medically induced coma following a sparring session in Denmark on 24 July.

Chapman had collapsed after training and was taken to hospital after Scott called for an ambulance, to be later diagnosed with a brain haematoma and cerebral oedema.

"I remember the final spar where it happened, It was the third spar of the week and I felt fine going in there," she told BBC South Today.

"It was just a sort of freak injury that I never thought it would happen to me, we (herself and Scott) have done hundreds of sparring rounds together and my fights.

"He knows the kind of things that I say and I wasn't acting myself from what he said, that's when he called an ambulance before anything even happened.

"I sat down and then it all sort of happened after that, luckily with where I was at the time, I think in under an hour from when the ambulance was called I was then into surgery."

After reaching hospital, the procedure Chapman underwent successfully stemmed the bleeding in her brain and helped to stabilise the swelling.

A fundraiser was then launched online for people to contribute towards getting her back to the UK and her long-term recovery.

A total of £97,792 was donated after the page was shared widely among the boxing community on social media.

Chapman's promoters Queensberry, Matchroom Boxing's Eddie Hearn and Most Valuable Promotions' Nakisa Bidarian were among the leading donors.

"All the support that I got was just amazing," Chapman added.

"That's why, with all the fundraising money, I'm going to use that to make sure I'm getting everything so that I get better as that's why people donated.

"It brings a tear to your eye when you see it and how much people are there for you in the community, it's a special world, the boxing world."

Chapman 'gutted' at not being able to achieve dreams

Norwich-born Chapman trains at Warriors Gym in High Wycombe and as a professional won 10 of her 12 fights with just two defeats.

At one stage of her career she was based in Bournemouth, training alongside former WBO cruiserweight champion Chris Billam-Smith, who was one of many professional boxers to share a video message of support for her.

Chapman lost to Skye Nicolson in a bid to win the WBC featherweight belt in October 2024 , the only women's world title fight ever to be held in Saudi Arabia.

She admitted that not being able to now achieve what she had hoped in the sport will to be difficult to come to terms with.

"I probably would never get a licence again after this," Chapman said.

"Even if they said I could, I probably wouldn't want to risk putting my loved ones through that pain of it again.

"I'm gutted that I'm not going to achieve the dreams I did have, which I knew I would be able to achieve, but it is what it is.

"Maybe one day I'll help other boxers achieve those dreams, I've still got a bit of time before I decide exactly what it is I can do and see where I want to be."

Having initially been wheelchair-bound in the early stages of her recovery, Chapman finally managed to lace up a pair of gloves again this week.

Although her days of competing in the ring may be over, she can still enjoy some aspects of the sport as she continues into the next stage of her life.

"I loved it, I think I smiled my whole way through it," she added.

"As much as I may never spar again or fight again, I can still do the craft and hit the pads and hit the bags and enjoy it."

articles.title: Boxing fan favorite Amanda Serrano announces 'The Last Walk' fight in home country of Puerto Rico
articles.summary: Amanda Serrano will face Skye Falzon on Jan. 9 in Puerto Rico for her final bout, capping a historic career that transformed women's boxing.
articles.body: One of the greatest boxers of all time is hanging up the gloves. World featherweight champion Amanda Serrano and Most Valuable Promotions, co-founded by Jake Paul, announced that Serrano will have her "Last Walk" on Jan. 9 against Skye Falzon in her home country of Puerto Rico. "Boxing has been my life, and I never could have imagined the journey it would take me and my family on. From the early days when women's boxing was fighting for recognition in small theater shows, to headlining Madison Square Garden in New York, reaching millions of fans around the world on the biggest shows, and helping open doors for the next generation of female fighters, [husband] Jordan [Maldonado] and I always believed and I'm proud of everything we've accomplished... CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "To close my career at home in Puerto Rico, in front of the people who have supported me from the beginning, means everything. On Saturday, January 9, I'm going to give the fans one final night to remember. This is The Last Walk of my boxing career, and I hope everyone who has been part of this journey, from Puerto Rico and New York to fans watching around the world... will be there to share it with me." Serrano also praised Paul and his MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian for helping her pave the way for women's boxing. "Nakisa, Jake and MVP believed in me and in women's boxing, and together we've helped change what's possible for women in this sport. We've fought for respect, equal opportunities, fair pay, and the choice to compete under the same rules as men. There's still more work to do, and I'll continue fighting for the next generation long after I hang up my gloves." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER "Amanda Serrano is the MOAT. The Most Of All Time. The most accomplished female boxer of all time, the most watched, the most paid, and one of the most influential athletes this sport has ever seen," Paul and Bidarian said. "When Amanda became MVP's first signee, we made a commitment to build a platform where the greatest female fighters in the world could receive the recognition, compensation and opportunities they deserve. Amanda has been the foundation of that vision, and her success has helped change the entire landscape of women's boxing. Together, we've shattered records, delivered some of the biggest events in combat sports history and proven that women's boxing belongs on the world's biggest stages. "The Last Walk is a celebration of an athlete who changed the sport forever, and alongside DAZN who has supported women’s boxing’s biggest events time and time again, we're proud to give Amanda the farewell she deserves. Saturday, January 9, will mark the end of an extraordinary career inside the ring, but Amanda's legacy will live on through every female fighter who follows in her footsteps." Serrano had already made a name for herself in the boxing world but gained worldwide popularity when her second fight against Katie Taylor was the co-main event of Jake Paul vs. Mike Tyson in November 2024. Serrano lost all three of her fights to Taylor by decision, two of which were main events at a sold-out Madison Square Garden. articles.title: El español Mattia Giordano ficha por Cage Warriors
articles.standfirst: El menorquín debutará este 7 de noviembre en el 'Spanish Showcase' de Londres
articles.summary: El menorquín debutará este 7 de noviembre en el 'Spanish Showcase' de Londres
articles.body: Otro español más para la 'spanish army' de Cage Warriors. El menorquín Mattia Giordani (5-2), compañero de equipo del UFC Fabià Sintes, peleará en la histórica promotora británica y debutará el 7 de noviembre, en el 'Spanish Showcase' que tendrá lugar en los antiguos estudios de la BBC, en Londres. Giordano, que está en una racha de tres triunfos consecutivos y viene de sorprender al mundo ganando en PFL Madrid a Ernesto 'El Potro' Schisano (5-2), se medirá la francés Maximilien Vallot (7-6). Vallot también debutará en Cage Warriors aunque ya en su día pudo haber peleado... ¡ante el UFC Lone'er Kavanagh!. Sin embargo, esa pelea se canceló e hizo después carrera en Hexagone MMA, en Francia. Mattia Giordano se une a la larga lista de españoles que estarán en el 'Spanish Showcase' de Cage Warriors: Manuel del Valle (8-1), Paddy Rutdledge (3-1), Arturo Izquierdo, Angel Bellucci (2-1-1) y Samuel Blasco (14-17-1).

articles.title: Canelo Alvarez would tarnish his legacy if he lost to Christian Mbilli on Saturday, says former opponent Matthew Hatton
articles.summary: Canelo Alvarez is putting his legacy at risk if he loses to Christian Mbilli warns Matthew Hatton; the Mexican superstar fought Hatton in 2011 in the first world title of Canelo's outstanding career; he is coming back from defeat to Terence Crawford to fight Mbilli for WBC title in Riyadh
articles.body:
Hatton, the brother of British boxing legend Ricky, was a European champion and world-level contender in his own career.

He boxed Canelo back in 2011, in the first world title fight of the Mexican superstar's career.

"When I agreed to the fight he was being billed as the next big superstar in world boxing," Hatton told the Toe2Toe podcast. "There was a lot of hype surrounding him and the build-up was fantastic.

"It's easy to underestimate people when they're so young and I think I possibly did that a little bit. His shot selection, his punch-picking, his variety for such a young man was really, really good. His boxing IQ for someone so young was remarkable really.

"When you look at his record, the amount of fights he's had at the very top level, it's absolutely incredible really. He's a modern-day great."

But Hatton believes it is now time for Canelo to retire with his legacy secure.

"Personally I would like to see Canelo stop now, he's had such a good career, he's had a fantastic legacy and I think it's a shame when they go on too long," Hatton said.

Canelo is returning from defeat to Terence Crawford to box Christian Mbilli for the WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh on Saturday.

"I do think he's still got enough left to beat Mbilli. I think it's an interesting fight," Hatton noted, but warned: "I know people say it doesn't tarnish their legacy but for me, slightly, it does. Say he was to lose to Mbilli on the weekend for me it does tarnish that a little bit.

"We all look at that differently. I would like to see him retire now."

Canelo is going ahead with his fight against Mbilli in Saudi Arabia amid escalating conflict in the region.

Houthi attacks have targeted Saudi airports, including Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, while security concerns have led to the postponement or cancellation of other sporting events in the kingdom.

"You know, fighting in Saudi for me is special and whatever it takes I'm going to be a world champion again," Canelo has said.

"Because I'm a fighter and I want to achieve a lot of things in boxing yet and that motivates myself. I love boxing."

articles.title: World Wrestling Championships: India script history as Neelam Sirohi, Kajal Dhochak settle for silver
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With 30 seconds left and the scores locked at 4-4, Kajal Dhochak stood on the brink of a golden finish.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With 30 seconds left and the scores locked at 4-4, Kajal Dhochak stood on the brink of a golden finish. The 18-year-old Indian had fought her way back into contention, but just when victory appeared within reach, Ukraine’s Anastasiya Alpyeyeva struck decisively. Kajal’s spirited resistance ended in an agonising 6-8 defeat in the women’s 76kg final at the World Wrestling Championships in Astana on Wednesday.The heartbreak, however, could not overshadow a landmark day for Indian wrestling. Kajal and Neelam Sirohi claimed silver medals, becoming the first Indian women to reach the finals of the same edition of the senior Worlds.Kajal, competing at the senior Worlds for the first time, began the final on the back foot, trailing 1-3 after the opening three-minute period. She regrouped impressively in the second half, clawing her way back to level the contest at 4-4.With the bout finely poised, Alpyeyeva, a two-time European champion, executed a crucial move and exposure angle to establish an 8-4 advantage. Kajal managed a late takedown, but the deficit proved insurmountable.The silver capped an impressive campaign for the teenager, a two-time under-20 world champion, who had produced a stunning 10-7 comeback victory over Kyrgyzstan’s Aiperi Medet Kyzy after trailing 1-7 in the semifinals.Earlier, Neelam faced arguably the toughest examination of her career against Japan’s Yui Susaki, one of freestyle wrestling’s most accomplished champions, in the women’s 50kg final.The 26-year-old Indian, who had defeated Kazakhstan’s Zeinep Bayanova 7-3 to reach the title clash, encountered an opponent operating at an extraordinary level. Susaki established a 5-0 lead before pinning Neelam towards the end of the opening period, sealing another world title without conceding a point throughout her tournament campaign.The victory secured Susaki’s fifth World Championships crown. The Japanese star had previously won gold once in the 48kg category and three times at 50kg, underlining her sustained dominance.For Neelam, the silver was a significant breakthrough after missing out on an Asian Games selection spot earlier this year.Until now, Anshu Malik’s silver in the 57kg category at the 2021 Worlds in Oslo had stood alone as an Indian woman’s runner-up finish at the senior championships.Neelam and Kajal have now changed that narrative, delivering an impressive double-silver finish to strengthen the nation's growing presence in women’s wrestling.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Prates y Morales ya calientan su pelea: "Puedo seguir fumando..."
articles.standfirst: Ambos peleadores se enfrentarán el 31 de enero con el cinturón interino de peso wélter en juego
articles.summary: Ambos peleadores se enfrentarán el 31 de enero con el cinturón interino de peso wélter en juego
articles.body: El pasado sábado, la UFC sorprendió al anunciar la cartelera del UFC 336 que se celebrará en Toronto el próximo 31 de enero. Más allá del duelo por el título de peso mosca entre Joshua Van y Manel Kape, lo que más llamó la atención es el enfrentamiento entre Carlos Prates y Michael Morales por el cinturón interino de peso wélter, tras la negativa de Islam Makhachev -campeón indiscutido- de medirse al brasileño antes del Ramadán. Entre ambos peleadores ya había beef previo, algo que se ha intensificado tras el anuncio oficial. Desde hace meses, Partes y Morales son considerados los dos principales retadores al cinturón de la división, y ahora solo puede quedar uno. Cuando Makhachev venció a Ian Garry el pasado agosto en el UFC 330, ambos estuvieron presentes e intercambiaron mensajes, aunque parecía ser Carlos el que tenía la delantera y le decía a Michael que le noquearía una vez consiguiese el cinturón. El propio Islam afirmó que 'The Nighmare' se merecía ser el próximo retador, pero ha dado un paso atrás y ha preferido que se decida en una pelea eliminatoria. El primero en lanzar su ataque tras el anuncio fue Morales, que le dijo a Prates que "me has llamado cobarde, ¿pero has necesitado diez meses para prepararte para pelear conmigo? Ahora cierra el pico y deja de fumar, porque créeme, vas a necesitar los pulmones". Obviamente, la respuesta de Prates no se hizo esperar, y le dijo que "no te preocupes, puedo seguir fumando. Solo necesito dos asaltos para noquearte". Sin duda, toda una declaración de intenciones del que probablemente sea el striker más temido de la categoría, que en esta ocasión se medirá a un portento físico que tiene poder de K.O. y el as bajo la manga de poder llevar el combate al terreno de la lucha. Curiosamente, la última vez que ambos coincidieron en una cartelera fue también la ultima aparición de Morales. Esto sucedió en noviembre de 2025, cuando el ecuatoriano noqueó a Sean Brady en el primer asalto en el Madison Square Garden y el brasileño hizo lo propio en el segundo ante todo un ex campeón como Leon Edwards. Desde aquel momento, Michael ha esperado con paciencia a que llegase la oportunidad, mientras que 'The Nighmare' ha preferido mantenerse activo, noqueando a otro ex campeón como Jack Della Maddalena. Cualquiera de los dos es una gran amenaza para Makhachev, por lo que en tres meses se disiparán las dudas y se conocerá quién el próximo contendiente al cinturón de la categoría, además del nuevo campeón interino.
